SplitPanel from ui-components shows two panes, side by side or one above the other, with a divider between them. Drag the divider with the mouse, a pen or a finger to share the space differently; or give it the focus with Tab and move it with the arrow keys, take it to its limits with Home and End. A double click takes it back to where it started. The buttons on a collapsible divider hide a pane, giving the other all the space, and show it again; Enter does so from the keyboard. Split panels go in each other's panes: the layout below is two of them, the files beside an editor above its console.

Sizes are in percent or in pixels. The files are 220 pixels wide, from 140 pixels to half the width, and keep their width when the window changes; the editor takes 65 percent of the height, and leaves the console at least 60 pixels. The divider moves in the browser, between those limits. With setSendToServer the browser sends each change via Ajax, and the sentence below the layout follows. Where the panel keeps it is its model: the files' split panel keeps it in the session, so the page shows it again when you open it anew; the editor's in the page, as by default. The check boxes render the third split panel again by Ajax. Everything works under a strict Content Security Policy, without inline style.
Side by side or one above the other
The files take {0} of the width, the editor {1} of the height.
The first pane: on the left, or on top.
The second pane: on the right, or below.
